facts.statement: The genus Supersaurus was formally described by James A. Jensen in 1985.
facts.quote: authority: Jensen, 1985

facts.statement: Supersaurus lived in North America during the Late Jurassic period.
facts.quote: lived in North America during the Late Jurassic period

facts.statement: The type species, Supersaurus vivianae, was first discovered by Vivian Jones in Colorado in 1972.
facts.quote: first discovered by Vivian Jones of Delta, Colorado, in the middle Morrison Formation of Colorado in 1972

facts.statement: The fossils of Supersaurus date between 153 and 145 million years ago.
facts.quote: dating between 153 and 145 million years ago

facts.statement: Mass estimates for the known Supersaurus specimens range from 35 to 44 metric tons.
facts.quote: Mass estimates for the WDC and BYU specimens tend to be around 35 - 44 MT in body mass

facts.statement: The original fossil remains of Supersaurus were found at the Dry Mesa Quarry in 1972.
facts.quote: The original fossil remains of Supersaurus were discovered in the Dry Mesa Quarry in 1972

facts.statement: The name "Supersaurus" was used informally from 1973 but was not officially published until 1985.
facts.quote: The specimen was given the name "Supersaurus" informally as early as 1973, but was not officially described and named until more than a decade later, in 1985

facts.statement: A more complete specimen, WDC DMJ-021, was discovered in Wyoming in 1986 by Brandon Flyr and Bart Lesco.
facts.quote: A much more complete specimen WDC DMJ-021, was found in Converse County, Wyoming in 1986 by Brandon Flyr and Bart Lesco

facts.statement: The name Ultrasauros is now considered a junior synonym of Supersaurus because Supersaurus was named first.
facts.quote: Therefore, Ultrasauros became a junior synonym of Supersaurus, which had been named first and thus retains priority

facts.statement: The genus Dystylosaurus is now considered a junior synonym of Supersaurus.
facts.quote: Hence, Dystylosaurus has also become a junior synonym of Supersaurus

facts.statement: The WDC and BYU specimens of Supersaurus are estimated to weigh between 35 and 44 metric tons.
facts.quote: The WDC and BYU specimens are estimated to have weighed 35 - 44 MT in body mass

facts.statement: Despite unreliable dating methods, the "Jimbo" specimen is considered possibly the oldest known dinosaur.
facts.quote: Thus, despite the lack of a truly reliable age value, the Jimbo specimen of Supersaurus can be considered as possibly the oldest dinosaur known thus far

facts.statement: Michael Benton agreed that the BYU 9024 vertebra belongs to Supersaurus, suggesting the animal could reach 50 meters in length.
facts.quote: Michael Benton also agreed with the reclassification, giving the Supersaurus BYU 9024 specimen an approximate length of up to an impressive 50 m

facts.statement: The WDC DMJ-021 specimen shows that Supersaurus was similar to Apatosaurus but less robust, with exceptionally long neck vertebrae.
facts.quote: The assignment of the more complete specimen, WDC DMJ-021, to Supersaurus suggests that in most respects it was very similar in anatomy to Apatosaurus but less robustly built with especially elongated cervical vertebrae

facts.statement: Most studies initially placed Supersaurus in the subfamily Diplodocinae due to its relation to Barosaurus, but later research based on the WDC DMJ-021 specimen reclassified it as a close relative of Apatosaurus within the subfamily Apatosaurinae.
facts.quote: Originally, it was thought that Supersaurus was related to the long-necked diplodocid Barosaurus, and therefore a member of the subfamily Diplodocinae, however, with the assignment of the more complete WDC DMJ-021 most later studies found Supersaurus to be a close relative of the familiar Apatosaurus in the group Apatosaurinae.

facts.statement: The genus Supersaurus was named and described by Jensen in 1985.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Jensen, 1985

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Supersaurus is Supersaurus vivianae.
facts.quote: type_species: Supersaurus vivianae

facts.statement: Supersaurus has had several synonyms including Dystylosaurus, Ultrasauros, Dinehirosaurus, and Jensenosaurus.
facts.quote: synonyms: Dystylosaurus Jensen, 1985 Ultrasauros Olshevsky, 1991 Dinehirosaurus Bonaparte & Mateus, 1999 "Jensenosaurus" Olshevsky, 1996

facts.statement: Supersaurus lived during the late Jurassic period, approximately 155.7 to 150.8 million years ago, in what is now North America and possibly Europe.
facts.quote: Supersaurus ("Super lagarto") fue un género representado por dos especies de dinosaurios saurópodos diplodócidos que vivieron a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 155,7 y 150,8 millones de años, entre el Kimmeridgiense y el Titoniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica y posiblemente Europa.

facts.statement: Supersaurus is among the largest diplodocids and is possibly the longest sauropod known from well-preserved remains.
facts.quote: Encontrándose entre los mayores diplodócidos, y posiblemente es el saurópodo más largo hasta ahora conocido por restos bien preservados.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence estimates Supersaurus to have been 32 to 34 meters long and weighed between 35 and 40 tonnes.
facts.quote: Las evidencias fósiles han dado a estimar a esta especie de saurópodo con una longitud de 32 a 34 metros y un peso de entre 35 y 40 toneladas.

facts.statement: Like typical diplodocids, Supersaurus had a small skull, sturdy legs, and long neck and tail.
facts.quote: Como todo diplodócido típico, tenía un cráneo pequeño, patas macizas y cuello y cola largas.

facts.statement: Supersaurus had a slightly less robust build than Apatosaurus and possessed much longer cervical vertebrae, resulting in a proportionally longer neck.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, hubiese tenido una contextura general un poco menos robusta, y otra diferencia fueron sus vértebras cervicales, que eran mucho más alargadas, lo que resultaría en un cuello proporcionalmente más largo en comparación a Apatosaurus.

facts.statement: The first remains of Supersaurus consisted of a few bones, including a 2.4-meter-long scapulocoracoid holotype and some neck vertebrae found in the Morrison Formation of Colorado, USA.
facts.quote: Los primeros restos de Supersaurus fueron solo unos pocos huesos: una cintura escapular o escapulocoracoide de cerca de 2,4 metros de largo es el holotipo, BYU 5500) y algunas vértebras del cuello encontradas en la Formación Morrison de Colorado, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: A more complete specimen nicknamed 'Jimbo' was discovered in Converse County, Wyoming, USA.
facts.quote: Un nuevo y más completo espécimen de Supersaurus, apodado 'Jimbo', fue encontrado en el condado de Converse, Wyoming Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: The original fossil remains of Supersaurus were discovered at the Dry Mesa Quarry in 1972.
facts.quote: Los restos fósiles originales de Supersaurus fueron descubiertos en la Cantera Dry Mesa en 1972.

facts.statement: Paleontologist James A. Jensen described Supersaurus and designated a scapulocoracoid (originally labeled BYU 5500) as the type specimen.
facts.quote: El paleontólogo James A. Jensen describió a Supersaurus, designó un escapulocoracoides BYU 9025, originalmente etiquetado como BYU 5500, como el espécimen tipo.

facts.statement: The name "Supersaurus" was used informally as early as 1973, but the genus was not officially described or named until 1985.
facts.quote: El espécimen recibió el nombre de "Supersaurus" de manera informal ya en 1973, pero no se describió ni nombró oficialmente hasta más de una década después, en 1985.

facts.statement: A much more complete specimen, WDC DMJ-021, was found in Converse County, Wyoming, in 1986 by Brandon Flyr and Bart Lesco while they were walking.
facts.quote: Un espécimen mucho más completo, WDC DMJ-021, fue encontrado en el condado de Converse, Wyoming en 1986 por Brandon Flyr y Bart Lesco mientras caminaban y se informó a las personas que poseían la tierra en ese momento.

facts.statement: A diplodocid found near the original Supersaurus site, known only by a dorsal vertebra (BYU 5750), was named Dystylosaurus edwini but is now considered a specimen of Supersaurus vivianae.
facts.quote: Otro dinosaurio diplodócido encontrado cerca del yacimiento original del Supersaurus, conocido solo por una vértebra dorsal, BYU 5750, fue llamado Dystylosaurus edwini y hoy es considerado un espécimen de Supersaurus vivianae.

facts.statement: A possible second species, S. lourinhanensis, originally described as Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis in 1999 by Bonaparte and Mateus, is known from Portugal and dated to a similar time period.
facts.quote: Una posible segunda especie, S. lourinhanensis que fue originalmente descrita como Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis en 1999 por Bonaparte y Mateus, se conoce en Portugal y se ha fechado en una época similar.

facts.statement: Anatomically, Supersaurus was very similar to Apatosaurus, featuring a robust and deep chest due to wide ribs and a thickened neck.
facts.quote: En la mayoría de los aspectos anatómicos, Supersaurus era muy similar a Apatosaurus, con un pecho robusto y profundo debido a sus amplias costillas y un engrosado cuello.

facts.statement: James A. Jensen originally described Supersaurus and simultaneously reported a giant sauropod he later named Ultrasaurus macintoshi, which was subsequently renamed Ultrasauros macintoshi.
facts.quote: El paleontólogo James A. Jensen, quien describió originalmente al espécimen de Supersaurus, simultáneamente reportó el descubrimiento de otro saurópodo gigante, al que más tarde llamó "Ultrasaurus" macintoshi posteriormente renombrado Ultrasauros macintoshi.

facts.statement: The type specimen used to define Ultrasauros was a dorsal vertebra cataloged as BYU 9044, which was later proven to belong to Supersaurus.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo usado para definir esta nueva de Ultrasauros, resultó ser una vértebra dorsal, catalogada como BYU 9044, que más tarde se demostró que pertenecía a Supersaurus.

facts.statement: Ultrasauros became a junior synonym of Supersaurus because the first name retains priority, leaving Ultrasauros aside.
facts.quote: De esta manera, Ultrasauros se transformó en sinónimo más moderno de Supersaurus, ya que el primer nombre mantiene la prioridad y el nombre Ultrasauros es dejado de lado.

facts.statement: Originally, Supersaurus and Brachiosaurus bones were thought to represent a single dinosaur measuring 25 to 30 meters long, 8 meters high at the shoulder, 15 meters in total height, and weighing around 70 tons.
facts.quote: Originalmente, estos huesos de Supersaurus y Brachiosaurus se pensaron que representaban a un solo dinosaurio que medía entre 25 a 30 metros de largo, 8 alto al hombro, 15 metros de altura total, y que quizás hubiera pesado alrededor de 70 toneladas.

facts.statement: Initially, mass estimates extended to 180 tons, placing it in the same category as the blue whale and the problematic titanosaur genus Bruhathkayosaurus.
facts.quote: En un principio, las estimaciones de la masa se extendieron hasta 180 toneladas, que lo colocaron en la misma categoría que el ballena azul y el problemático género de titanosaurio Bruhathkayosaurus.

facts.statement: Before Jim Jensen published his discovery in 1985, paleontologist Haang Mook Kim used the name Ultrasaurus in a 1983 publication to describe what he believed was a giant dinosaur in South Korea.
facts.quote: Antes que Jim Jensen publicara su descubrimiento en 1985, otro palentólogo, Haang Mook Kim, usó el nombre Ultrasaurus en una publicación de 1983 para describir lo que él creyó era un dinosaurio gigante en Corea del Sur.

facts.statement: Although the naming logic was incorrect, Kim's Ultrasaurus met the requirements for naming and would be the legitimate name, though the genus is doubtful.
facts.quote: Mientras que la lógica del nombramiento era incorrecta, el Ultrasaurus de Kim si satisfizo los requisitos para nombrar y sería el nombre legítimo, aunque el género es dudoso.

facts.statement: In 1991, on the suggestion of George Olshevsky, a letter was changed and Jensen retitled his sauropod as Ultrasauros.
facts.quote: En 1991, por sugerencia de George Olshevsky le fue cambiada una letra, y Jensen retituló a su saurópodo como Ultrasauros.

facts.statement: When it was later discovered that the new name referred to bones of two already known separate genera, the name Ultrasauros became a junior synonym for Supersaurus.
facts.quote: Cuando más adelante fue descubierto que el nuevo nombre se refería a los huesos de dos géneros separado ya conocidos, el nombre Ultrasauros se convirtió un sinónimo más moderno para Supersaurus.

facts.statement: Originally, Supersaurus was thought to be related to the long-necked diplodocid Barosaurus and thus a member of the subfamily Diplodocinae, however, with the assignment of the more complete WDC DMJ-021, most subsequent studies found that Supersaurus was a close relative of Apatosaurus in the group Apatosaurinae.
facts.quote: Originalmente, se pensó que Supersaurus estaba relacionado con el diplodócido de cuello largo Barosaurus y, por lo tanto, un miembro de la subfamilia Diplodocinae, sin embargo, con la asignación del más completo WDC DMJ-021, la mayoría de los estudios posteriores encontraron que Supersaurus era un pariente cercano del familiar Apatosaurus en el grupo Apatosaurinae.

facts.statement: However, some subsequent studies question this paradigm.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, algunos estudios posteriores ponen en duda este paradigma.

facts.statement: A comprehensive study of diplodocoidean relationships published by Whitlock in 2011 found that Apatosaurus itself was at the base of the diplodocid family tree, and that other "apatosaurines", including Supersaurus, were increasingly related to Diplodocus, making them diplodocines.
facts.quote: Un estudio exhaustivo de las relaciones diplodocoideas publicado por Whitlock en 2011 encontró que el propio Apatosaurus se encontraba en la base del árbol genealógico de los diplodocidos, y que otros "apatosaurinos", incluido Supersaurus , estaban cada vez más relacionados con Diplodocus, haciéndolos diplodocinos.

facts.statement: In 2015, in the review of diplodocid species by Tschopp and colleagues, it was found that Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis grouped with Supersaurus as a member of Apatosaurinae.
facts.quote: En 2015, en la revisión de las especies de diplodocídos de Tschopp y colegas, encontró que Dinheirosaurus lourinhanensis se agrupaba con Supersaurus como miembro de Apatosaurinae.

facts.statement: Supersaurus lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, between 154.8 and 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Supersaurus is Diplodocinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Diplodocinae

facts.statement: Supersaurus belongs to the family Diplodocidae.
facts.quote: Family: Diplodocidae

facts.statement: Supersaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: There are 5 recorded fossil occurrences of Supersaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 5
